representative_work: Patterns in Property Specifications for Finite-State Verification
formalism: LTL; CTL; QRE; GIL; INCA template mappings
input: Natural-language requirement plus a human-selected pattern, scope, and proposition bindings
output: An instantiated formal property in the selected target formalism
automation: Human-guided template selection with deterministic instantiation
semantic_guarantee: Each catalog entry has a precise intent and fixed formal mappings; correctness of choosing the pattern and grounding propositions remains a human responsibility
evaluation_evidence: The authors surveyed more than 500 collected specifications and reported that most were pattern instances; they did not provide a controlled end-user correctness study
strengths: Small auditable vocabulary; deterministic generation; explicit scopes; strong source-to-formula traceability
failures: Untimed base catalog; no automatic free-text interpretation; proposition grounding and uncommon requirements remain manual; template choice can be wrong
tafuzz_role: Use as the deterministic core of a TAFuzz-Req pattern compiler and as the manual gold baseline
status_notes: Primary publication and maintained catalog verified; foundational work outside the recent-review window

input: Timing-dependent embedded-system requirement plus a human-selected scope and real-time category
output: Structured-English requirement and parameterized real-time temporal-logic formulas
automation: Human-guided selection with deterministic template mapping
semantic_guarantee: Predefined mappings give a precise meaning once a pattern is selected; the paper does not prove automatic interpretation of unrestricted prose
evaluation_evidence: Patterns were derived from industrial automotive and appliance requirements and illustrated on a real automotive embedded-system example; no NL-to-formula precision or recall was reported
strengths: Adds duration, periodicity, and real-time ordering to qualitative patterns; close conceptual match to bounded protocol deadlines
failures: Some templates use punctual or logic-specific constructs outside strict MITL; AP definitions and interval endpoint choices remain manual
tafuzz_role: Use as the timed template library, after restricting templates to the exact MightyPPL MITL/past/Pnueli grammar and timed-word semantics
status_notes: Publication verified; the PSP site links the real-time extension, but no standalone maintained compiler artifact was verified

method_family: Controlled natural language and verified templates
representative_work: Automated Formalization of Structured Natural Language Requirements (FRET/FRETish)
formalism: Future- and past-time metric LTL/MTL over finite and infinite traces; FRETish uses discrete natural-number trace indices
input: A FRETish requirement with scope, condition, component, timing, and response fields plus user-provided variable mappings
output: Temporal formulas, precise English explanation, diagrams, simulation artifacts, and verification-tool translations
automation: Automatic after the author rewrites the requirement in FRETish and supplies model-variable mappings
semantic_guarantee: Template semantics is grounded in RTGIL and checked by generated traces; a later PVS development proves equivalence between FRETish denotation and generated past-time MTL
evaluation_evidence: Applied to the Lockheed Martin CPS challenge; the 2022 CPP work gives a machine-checked compositional correctness proof; this is evidence for the controlled-language compiler, not free-NL extraction accuracy
strengths: Strongest assurance among authoring approaches; compositional templates; explanations and simulation support human review
failures: Not a free-text extractor; users initially need help; discrete step semantics and punctual intervals can differ from TAFuzz timestamped MITL; model/AP mappings are still manual
tafuzz_role: Reuse the field schema, explanations, and boundary-test idea; implement a smaller TAFuzz-specific CNL/compiler instead of accepting FRET output without a semantics adapter
status_notes: Paper, proof, and official repository verified; direct semantic compatibility with MightyPPL must be established separately

representative_work: ARSENAL: Automatic Requirements Specification Extraction from Natural Language
formalism: First-order logic; LTL; SAL transition-system models
output: Intermediate logical relations, FOL/LTL formulas, and analyzable SAL models
automation: Automated pipeline after domain preprocessing and rule tuning
semantic_guarantee: Downstream consistency, satisfiability, and realizability checks can reject some bad results, but there is no proof that extracted formulas preserve sentence meaning
evaluation_evidence: Across 300 sentences, 112 were used to tune rules and 188 were held out; the reported NLP-stage F-measure on the held-out set was 0.63 (TTE 0.65, Eurail 0.58, GPCA 0.62, LTLMop 0.64)
strengths: Interpretable relations and rewrite rules; can exploit domain syntax; produces analyzable models rather than opaque embeddings
failures: Dependency-parser failures can delete whole clauses; domain n-grams and preprocessing require maintenance; output is untimed LTL/FOL rather than MITL
tafuzz_role: Use only for candidate clause, actor, event, and AP extraction; never use its raw logical output as the TAFuzz oracle
status_notes: Primary technical report and metrics verified; a maintained official artifact was not verified

representative_work: nl2spec: Interactively Translating Unstructured Natural Language to Temporal Logics with Large Language Models
formalism: LTL in the evaluated benchmark; an STL example is provided as a proof of concept
input: One-sentence unstructured natural-language requirements and a declared atomic-proposition vocabulary
output: Temporal formula plus clause/subformula translations, alternatives, and confidence values
automation: LLM-generated initial translation with iterative human editing of subtranslations
semantic_guarantee: No semantic proof; correctness is established by expert judgment and interactive correction
evaluation_evidence: On 36 expert-created difficult LTL instances, initial Codex accuracy was 44.4% with the minimal prompt and 58.3% with in-distribution examples; 15 of 20 initially wrong cases were corrected within at most three loops, averaging 1.86 loops
strengths: Makes ambiguity and local formula errors visible; human edits small subtranslations instead of rewriting a whole formula
failures: Initial accuracy is insufficient for an unattended oracle; tiny one-sentence benchmark; model and prompt dependent; no demonstrated RFC-to-MITL grounding
tafuzz_role: Use its subtranslation interaction pattern for LLM-assisted IR completion and review, but compile accepted IR deterministically to MITL
status_notes: Peer-reviewed paper, benchmark figures, and repository verified; evaluated evidence is primarily LTL, not MITL

representative_work: NL2TL: Transforming Natural Languages to Temporal Logics using Large Language Models
formalism: Primarily lifted/full STL in the reported pipeline, with LTL-derived navigation data normalized into the target representation
input: English instructions, optionally separated into lifted logical structure and domain-specific atomic propositions
output: Lifted temporal-logic structure or grounded full STL
automation: GPT-3-assisted corpus generation, expert correction, T5 fine-tuning, and a separate AP-recognition/grounding stage
semantic_guarantee: No formal semantic guarantee; evaluation uses exact binary formula accuracy against annotated targets
evaluation_evidence: The authors report about 28,000 NL-TL pairs; top-1 accuracy reached 97.52% on GPT-assisted test data and 90.12% on manual test data; human correction improved accuracy by about 10 percentage points
strengths: Correctly separates logical lifting from AP grounding; data-efficient domain adaptation; exposes grounding as an independent problem
failures: Mostly synthetic or curated sentence distributions; exact-match scores do not prove RFC intent; target is STL rather than TAFuzz MITL; direct GPT accuracy drops with more APs
tafuzz_role: Use as design evidence for a two-stage lifted-pattern plus deterministic-AP-dictionary architecture, not as a drop-in translator
status_notes: Preprint and reported metrics verified; an official maintained code/data URL was not independently verified

input: 1,580 pages of cleaned RFC text covering 14 protocols
automation: Chunked RFC prompting evaluated across nine open and commercial LLMs
semantic_guarantee: No formal semantic guarantee; 108 states and 297 transitions were manually validated and scoring allows structure-aware fuzzy partial matches
evaluation_evidence: Best state extraction reached 0.82 F1, while transition extraction was at most 0.38 F1, demonstrating a large state-transition gap
strengths: Current, reproducible benchmark for long technical documents; directly measures state, transition, alias, and event/action extraction
failures: Long-context reasoning, alias resolution, and coherent graph assembly remain weak; it extracts PSMs rather than temporal properties
tafuzz_role: Use as negative evidence against one-shot RFC-to-MITL generation and as a source of hard cases for section retrieval, coreference, and event/state dictionaries
artifact: Official paper page links paper and supplemental material; standalone repository URL not independently verified
status_notes: Peer-reviewed NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks work verified; adjacent evidence, not a MITL extractor

method_family: Hybrid RFC rule extraction and dynamic validation
representative_work: ProtocolGuard: Detecting Protocol Non-compliance Bugs via LLM-guided Static Analysis and Dynamic Verification
formalism: Structured normative-rule JSON, code slices, assertions, and executable protocol test seeds; not temporal logic
input: RFC specifications, RFC 2119 modal/comparison keywords, protocol terminology augmented by Wireshark dissectors, and implementation code
output: Context-complete rule records with request/response fields, rule-relevant code slices, assertions, and PoCs
automation: Keyword candidate filtering plus LLM keyword expansion, section-level coreference/context completion, schema-constrained JSON, static analysis, and fuzzing
semantic_guarantee: No rule-to-formula equivalence proof; suspected inconsistencies are checked by generated assertions, fuzzing, and manual review
evaluation_evidence: Extracted 420 rules across 11 implementations of 6 protocols; reported 181 inconsistencies, 158 confirmed bugs, and 90.6% overall precision; on four manually adjudicated programs the mean precision/recall was 86.3%/81.3%
strengths: Closest evidence for a scalable public-RFC-to-fuzzing pipeline; preserves section context and uses dynamic validation instead of trusting LLM output
failures: Authors report direct LLM rule extraction was inaccurate; callback/multi-transport code, long context, and LLM reasoning cause false positives/negatives; downstream bug metrics are not MITL extraction accuracy
tafuzz_role: Adopt its deterministic candidate retrieval and contextual structured IR; replace free-form assertion generation with a verified MITL template compiler and independent trace oracle
artifact: Artifact components are described in the paper appendix; public artifact URL not independently verified
status_notes: Peer-reviewed primary source verified; rule count and bug results must not be presented as formula-translation accuracy

representative_work: Automated Attack Synthesis by Extracting Finite State Machines from Protocol Specification Documents (RFCNLP)
formalism: XML-tagged protocol-independent IR, finite-state machines, and Promela; attack properties are hand-written LTL
input: RFC prose for BGPv4, DCCP, LTP, PPTP, SCTP, and TCP
output: Tagged states, events, variables, timers, triggers, actions, control flow, and an extracted FSM
automation: Technical-language pretraining, leave-one-protocol-out NeuralCRF/LinearCRF tagging, lexical matching, and rule-based IR-to-FSM construction
semantic_guarantee: No end-to-end semantic guarantee; even gold text annotations can miss transitions that are implicit, absent, or outside the grammar
evaluation_evidence: Phrase segmentation obtained 63.98 strict and 85.56 exact-boundary span scores; best NeuralCRF strict scores ranged from 57.34 to 87.34 by protocol; for TCP, 17 of 20 canonical transitions were recovered correctly or partially
strengths: Useful protocol-specific vocabulary and intermediate representation; explicitly models timers and control flow; tests zero-shot transfer to unseen protocols
failures: Ambiguity and omitted RFC information produce partial FSMs; canonical properties still required expert hand-writing; noisy models can accidentally satisfy properties for the wrong reason
tafuzz_role: Reuse event/state/timer lexicons and section annotations for AP and scope extraction only; do not treat the extracted FSM as an MITL property set
status_notes: Peer-reviewed publication and organization repository verified; this is FSM extraction, not automated temporal-property extraction

formalism: LTL interpreted on finite event traces with a user-supplied property-type template
input: A log containing multiple totally ordered event traces and an LTL template whose propositions are variables
output: All event bindings whose instantiated LTL formula holds on every input trace
automation: Automatic binding enumeration and optimized trace checking after a human supplies the template
semantic_guarantee: Sound and complete with respect to the selected template, the observed log, and Texada's finite-trace convention; no guarantee that a mined invariant is a normative requirement
evaluation_evidence: The evaluation reports operation on hundreds of traces with thousands of events per trace and that the map miner outperformed the specialized Synoptic miner in tested conditions; it does not report accuracy against intended requirements
strengths: Can discover recurring response/precedence relations and bind event names without free-text parsing; arbitrary LTL template structure
failures: Missing behaviors create false properties; vacuous truth and hundreds of candidates complicate review; untimed LTL cannot recover deadline bounds; observed implementation bugs may be learned as normal
tafuzz_role: Use only as an offline candidate-discovery and AP-relation tool on labeled/replayed traces; every candidate must be reconciled with an RFC source before becoming an oracle
artifact: Open-source Texada is stated in the paper; repository URL not independently re-verified
status_notes: Peer-reviewed method and primary PDF verified; exact repository provenance remains to be checked before packaging

representative_work: Transfer of Temporal Logic Formulas in Reinforcement Learning (Xu-Topcu)
formalism: Bounded MITLf in sequential disjunctive normal form over discrete time indices; primitive fragments use bounded eventually and always
input: Positive and negative labeled RL trajectories, a prior trajectory distribution, a classification threshold, and a formula-size threshold
output: An informative restricted MITLf formula and corresponding timed-automaton structures
automation: Automated search/inference over a restricted primitive grammar followed by logical-structure transfer
semantic_guarantee: The inferred formula is optimized for information gain while meeting a classification-rate constraint on supplied trajectories; this does not prove recovery of the task designer's true specification
evaluation_evidence: Two grid-world transfer case studies reported up to one order-of-magnitude sampling-efficiency gain from the extended state and up to another order from Q-function transfer; no cross-domain RFC extraction accuracy was evaluated
strengths: Actually infers metric interval bounds and MITL structure from labeled timed data; produces automata-compatible formulas
failures: Discrete-time and restricted SDNF fragment; Until is omitted; requires labeled desirable/undesirable trajectories and a prior; insufficient exploration yields incomplete or biased formulas
tafuzz_role: Use as an optional parameter/candidate miner and ablation baseline for timed traces, never as the authoritative source of RFC obligations
status_notes: Peer-reviewed primary source verified; method is task/trajectory inference rather than natural-language requirement extraction
